data.title: SpaceX Announces Date for Q3 2026 Earnings Report
data.description:
SpaceX has confirmed it will release its third-quarter 2026 financial and operational results on Tuesday, October 20, giving investors another look at the company’s performance following its first quarterly earnings report earlier this year.

The results will be published after market close, followed by a live audio-only webcast with SpaceX management at 3:30 p.m. CT (1:30 p.m. PT), where executives will discuss the company’s latest financial performance and operations.

SpaceX released its first quarterly earnings report in August, marking the first time the company shared its financial information.

That report covered the second quarter of 2026 and revealed revenue of $7.8 billion, alongside a net loss of $541 million. The figures provided an early look at the financial picture behind SpaceX’s rapidly expanding launch and satellite businesses.

According to an announcement published Friday, the company will make its results available through its Investor Relations website, where investors can also access the webcast and a replay afterward.

The presentation will also be livestreamed through SpaceX’s official account on X, making it accessible to anyone interested in following the results.

Investors will have an opportunity to submit questions ahead of the webcast through a dedicated Q&A platform.

Beyond the financial figures, the operational update will be worth watching. SpaceX continues to expand its Starlink satellite network while supporting a busy launch schedule, including missions carrying its own satellites and payloads for commercial and government customers.

The October 20 report should provide a clearer picture of how those operations contributed to SpaceX’s performance during the quarter, and whether the company has moved closer to profitability following its second-quarter loss.

data.title: Mercedes-Benz and NVIDIA expand partnership to develop next-generation autonomous driving
data.description:
Mercedes-Benz and NVIDIA are expanding their partnership to develop more advanced driver assistance and autonomous driving technology, with an eye on future SAE Level 4 systems.

Announced on Friday, the agreement builds on their existing partnership and combines Mercedes-Benz’s MB.OS operating system with NVIDIA’s latest artificial intelligence, computing, and safety technologies. The goal is to bring more capable automated driving features to future Mercedes vehicles, while laying the groundwork for future SAE Level 4 applications, including robolimousines.

The two companies first announced their partnership in 2020, with plans to develop a software-defined vehicle architecture capable of receiving new driving features through over-the-air updates.

Earlier this year, Mercedes-Benz also confirmed plans to use the new S-Class as the foundation for a Level 4 robotaxi service being developed with NVIDIA and Uber. The luxury sedan features redundant steering, braking, computing, and power systems designed to support driverless operation.

Under the expanded agreement, Mercedes’ MB.OS will work with NVIDIA Hyperion’s computing and sensor architecture, paired with NVIDIA’s Alpamayo Stack, a complete driving software package that uses AI reasoning to handle urban point-to-point assistance, active safety features, and automated parking.

NVIDIA’s Halos safety system will build on Mercedes-Benz’s existing safety systems, adding a second, parallel safety layer that provides redundancy and guardrails.

The partnership also extends beyond the vehicle, with Mercedes using NVIDIA technology for engineering simulations and digital manufacturing.

Neither Mercedes-Benz nor NVIDIA provided a timeline for the next generation of automated driving features.

data.title: 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLC Electric Arrives in Canada Starting at $78,400
data.description:
Mercedes-Benz has opened its Canadian configurator for the all-new 2027 GLC Electric, giving buyers their first opportunity to build and price the luxury electric SUV, following the Electric CLA’s Canadian launch earlier this year.

The GLC 400 4MATIC Electric launches with a starting starting price of $78,400, rising to $84,491 once fees and levies are included, according to the online configurator.

The electric GLC enters a competitive segment that includes the Tesla Model Y, BMW iX3, and Audi Q6 e-tron, offering impressive performance, fast charging, and a technology-heavy interior.

Mercedes-Benz GLC Canadian Pricing Comparison

Starting prices in Canadian dollars

2026 GLC 350e (PHEV) $66,900 $72,991
2027 GLC 400 4MATIC Electric $78,400 $84,491

Source: Mercedes-Benz Canada.

Unlike Mercedes-Benz’s earlier EQ-branded electric SUVs, the new GLC Electric adopts a familiar nameplate as the automaker moves toward offering electric and combustion-powered versions of its popular models.

At launch, Canadian buyers get a single model, the GLC 400 4MATIC Electric, with all-wheel drive producing a combined 483 horsepower and 590 lb-ft of torque. Mercedes-Benz claims the SUV can accelerate from 0 to 100 km/h in just 4.3 seconds.

Power comes from a 94 kWh usable battery, with an estimated driving range of 568 km to 715 km, according to Empty Tank. Official Natural Resources Canada range figures have not yet been released.

The GLC’s 800-volt architecture supports DC fast charging at up to 330 kW, allowing a 10% to 80% charge in approximately 22 minutes. Charging at 400-volt stations is limited to 100 kW.

Inside, buyers can add the massive 39.1-inch MBUX Hyperscreen for $1,800, although it requires the $2,300 Exclusive Trim. Other options include AMG styling, massaging front seats, and a Burmester sound system.

The SUV also offers up to 1,740 litres of cargo space, according to Driving.ca, and a 2,400 kg towing capacity.

Additional GLC Electric variants are expected to follow.

data.title: Slovakia becomes ninth EU country to officially approve Tesla FSD
data.description:
Slovakia has officially approved Tesla’s Full Self-Driving (FSD) Supervised system, joining the growing list of European Union countries to allow the advanced driver-assistance technology on public roads.

The country’s Ministry of Transport confirmed the decision on October 16, formally recognizing the provisional approval granted by Dutch regulator RDW in April. The move clears the regulatory hurdle for Tesla owners in Slovakia to begin using FSD, although Tesla has not confirmed when the software will become available.

The announcement comes just over a week after we reported that Slovakia was preparing to approve FSD. Transport Minister Jozef Ráž said at the time that the final paperwork was nearly complete.

Slovakia now joins the Netherlands, Lithuania, Estonia, Denmark, Belgium, Slovenia, Czechia, and Croatia in recognizing FSD. The approvals have been made possible by the Netherlands’ April 10 approval, which allows individual EU member states to recognize the system on their own territory while EU-wide approval is still pending.

In its announcement, Slovakia’s Transport Ministry highlighted FSD’s ability to navigate city streets and highways, including handling intersections, lane changes, traffic signals, acceleration, and braking.

Ráž also emphasized that the technology does not remove the driver’s responsibility. FSD remains a supervised system, requiring drivers to remain attentive and ready to intervene. According to the ministry, the system constantly monitors the driver’s attention, warning inattentive drivers and switching off if necessary.

The latest approval comes as Tesla continues pushing for broader European authorization. As previously reported, an EU-wide decision is now expected in December after regulators continued discussions rather than holding a vote earlier this month.

data.title: Zero-emission vehicle sales in Canada jump 55% in August as market share hits 13%
data.description:
Canada’s zero-emission vehicle (ZEV) market continued its recovery in August 2026, with sales climbing more than 55% compared to the same month last year, according to new figures released by Statistics Canada.

A total of 22,716 new ZEVs were sold during the month, accounting for 13.0% of all new vehicle sales nationwide. That’s a substantial improvement from August 2025, when zero-emission vehicles represented just 8.8% of the market.

Share of all new motor vehicle sales (%)

Year-over-year change: +4.2 percentage points

Source: Statistics Canada, New motor vehicle sales, August 2026 (October 15, 2026). Includes BEVs and PHEVs.

The increase comes as Canada’s EV market adjusts to changing government incentives. Earlier this year, the federal government introduced its new Electric Vehicle Affordability Program (EVAP), offering rebates of up to $5,000 on eligible electric vehicles. The program has helped bring several models back within reach of buyers, particularly when combined with manufacturer discounts.

According to Statistics Canada’s latest report, released October 15, overall new vehicle sales reached 174,611 units in August, an increase of 4.9% year-over-year. Sales revenue grew even faster, rising 8.8% compared to August 2025.

Zero-emission vehicles significantly outpaced that growth, with sales increasing 55.1% year-over-year. Their market share also climbed 4.2 percentage points, reflecting a stronger performance than the broader automotive market.

The gains weren’t limited to electric vehicles. Passenger car sales increased 14.2%, while truck sales rose a more modest 3.5%.

It’s important to note that Statistics Canada’s ZEV figures include both fully electric vehicles and plug-in hybrids, meaning the 22,716 total doesn’t represent battery-electric sales alone.

data.title: Waymo is coming to Canada, with Toronto robotaxi service planned for 2028
data.description:
Waymo is officially coming to Canada, announcing plans to launch its fully autonomous ride-hailing service in Toronto in 2028. The Alphabet-owned company will begin testing vehicles on Toronto streets in the coming days, marking its first expansion into the Canadian market.

As with its expansion into any new city, the initial phase will see Waymo vehicles driven manually to map local roads before progressing to autonomous testing with trained safety specialists behind the wheel. The company is also establishing local facilities and expects to create hundreds of jobs as it prepares for commercial operations.

Waymo has been steadily expanding its robotaxi network across the United States, while Tesla has been growing its own Robotaxi service since launching in Austin in June 2025.

Waymo partners with Canadian fleet operator

To support its Canadian launch, Waymo is expanding its partnership with Toronto-based Element Fleet Management, which already supports its operations in San Diego.

Element will oversee fleet maintenance, charging infrastructure, vehicle cleaning, and other daily operations needed to keep the robotaxis running.

Waymo says its autonomous vehicles have travelled more than 400 million kilometres without a human driver, with 95% fewer crashes involving serious injuries or worse compared to human drivers in its operating markets.

data.title: Global EV Sales Fall in September as Europe Hits Record Highs
data.description:
Global electric vehicle sales declined in September 2026, bringing an end to six consecutive months of growth as weaker demand in China and North America outweighed record-breaking sales in Europe.

According to data from Benchmark Mineral Intelligence reported by Reuters, global EV sales reached 2.15 million units in September, down 2% compared to the same month last year. Despite the decline, worldwide sales are still up 3% through the first nine months of 2026, reaching 15.5 million vehicles.

The slowdown comes as the EV market continues to adjust to changing government incentives. U.S. EV sales surged in the third quarter of 2025 as buyers rushed to take advantage of federal tax credits before they expired, making September 2025 a record month and creating a difficult comparison for automakers this year.

Canada has seen a different trend following the return of federal EV rebates in February. Registrations climbed 26.7% year over year in the second quarter, with 58,811 zero-emission vehicles registered, representing 10.7% of new vehicles.

Europe was September’s standout performer. Per Electrek‘s breakdown of the Benchmark data, sales climbed 39% to nearly 600,000 vehicles, a new monthly record. Germany recorded 117,000 sales, up 61%, while France jumped 78% to nearly 80,000. The UK, Spain, Portugal, and Finland also set monthly records.

China remained the largest market at 1.11 million vehicles, but sales fell 18% year over year. North America experienced an even sharper decline of 44%, with approximately 130,000 vehicles sold.

data.title: U.S. Built Vehicle Sales Slide in Canada as Tesla and Others Shift Production
data.description:
American-made vehicles are losing ground in Canada, with new data showing their share of the Canadian auto market dropped sharply during the first half of 2026 as tariffs forced automakers to rethink where they source their vehicles.

According to J.D. Power Canada data reported by The Globe and Mail, U.S.-built vehicles accounted for just 28.4% of new vehicle sales between January and June, down from 35.4% during the same period last year. That’s a 7-percentage-point decline, or nearly 20% of their previous market share.

Tesla has been one of the clearest examples of this shift. As Drive Tesla previously reported, the automaker moved Canadian Model Y supply from the United States to Giga Berlin to avoid Ottawa’s 25% counter-tariffs.

The change allowed Tesla to slash Model Y prices by $20,000. More recently, Tesla also began importing Shanghai-built Model 3 sedans under Canada’s new Chinese EV quota, which allows 49,000 vehicles annually at a 6.1% tariff.

The move was so popular Tesla forced the government’s hand to limit the number of vehicles Tesla could import over a fear they would leave none for other automakers.

Mexico and Japan Gain Market Share

The latest figures show Mexico benefiting significantly from these changes, with its share climbing from 18.3% to 22.2%, according to J.D. Power figures. Japan also gained ground, increasing from 13.7% to 16.6%, while South Korea rose from 14.6% to 15.6%.

Meanwhile, Canadian-built vehicles accounted for 11.5% of sales, down 9% year-over-year.

“Our data shows the largest change for vehicles coming out of the U.S.,” said Robert Karwel, director of OEM Solutions with J.D. Power in Canada.

Tesla isn’t alone. Mazda stopped Canadian sales of its Alabama-built CX-50, while Volvo halted imports of its South Carolina-built EX90.

Despite the decline, American-made vehicles still hold the largest individual share of Canada’s market. However, with tariffs remaining in place and manufacturers increasingly sourcing vehicles elsewhere, the shift away from U.S. production could continue into 2027.

data.title: Tesla Wants to Jump the Roadster Across Snake River Canyon in Evel Knievel-Inspired Stunt
data.description:
Tesla’s newly revealed Roadster could be headed for one of the most ambitious automotive stunts ever attempted. During Thursday’s unveiling at SpaceX’s McGregor, Texas test facility, Elon Musk suggested the company could attempt to fly the electric sports car across Idaho’s Snake River Canyon.

The idea would recreate Evel Knievel’s infamous 1974 attempt to cross the canyon, but this time using a Tesla Roadster equipped with a compressed-gas thruster system capable of lifting the vehicle off the ground.

Knievel’s original attempt involved a steam-powered rocket called the Skycycle X-2. The stunt ended in failure when its parachute deployed prematurely, sending Knievel down into the canyon. He survived, but the attempted jump became one of the most memorable moments of his career.

Tesla has spent years promising that its next-generation Roadster would offer capabilities beyond those of a conventional sports car. Those promises finally became reality during the October 15 unveiling, when the company demonstrated the Roadster flying twice in front of an audience.

Near the end of the livestream, Musk floated the possibility of taking things even further.

“So we’re going to have actually a follow-on demo… I don’t know if this is possible or not, but some people may know about Evel Knievel’s attempt to jump the Snake River Canyon.”

The response on stage was immediate: “Oh yeah, let’s give it another shot.”

The discussion then turned to speed. Tesla says the Roadster’s Rocket configuration can exceed 230 mph (370 km/h), but Musk suggested the canyon attempt could require something closer to Mach 0.5, roughly half the speed of sound.

“Where we’re going you don’t need tires,” Musk joked.

No date or specific plans were announced for the stunt. Tesla also hasn’t confirmed whether the idea will become an official demonstration.

For now, the company’s focus remains on bringing the Roadster into production in 2028.

data.title: Tesla Roadster’s Fan Suction System Generates Enough Downforce to Hold It Upside Down
data.description:
Tesla has revealed more details about the new Roadster‘s aerodynamic system, including powerful fans capable of generating enough suction to hold the electric sports car upside down while stationary.

Unveiled on on Thursday night, the next-generation Roadster combines a ground-effect suction system, active aerodynamics, and SpaceX-inspired cold-gas thrusters. Tesla says the technology will allow the car to achieve extraordinary levels of traction and cornering performance, even at low speeds.

The Roadster has been one of Tesla’s most anticipated vehicles since its original unveiling in 2017. Elon Musk has repeatedly promised performance beyond conventional sports cars, including a SpaceX package that would use thrusters to improve acceleration and handling. Now, nearly nine years later, Tesla has provided its clearest explanation yet of how those technologies work together.

Downforce Without Speed

Unlike traditional aerodynamic systems that rely on airflow generated by vehicle speed, the Roadster uses powered fans to pull air from underneath the car, as we first saw in a patent earlier this year. Combined with seals around the underbody, the system creates suction that pushes the vehicle against the road.

“We have a fan suction system on the bottom of the car that can pull up to two g’s in order to make the car go upside down. And then we borrowed some technology from SpaceX to do the rest,” Musk explained during the unveiling.

Tesla says the system can generate enough downforce to support cornering forces exceeding 2 g, compared with the roughly 1.26 g typically available from the tires alone.

During the demonstration on Thursday night, the system generated over 4,700 kg of downforce, enough to keep it stuck to the “road” while upside down.

The suction system operates in two modes, increasing traction at low speeds before opening front and rear airflow passages to improve performance at higher speeds.

The Roadster also features an adjustable rear wing, with actuators derived from Tesla’s Optimus robot program. Its angle changes automatically to balance downforce and aerodynamic drag.

Meanwhile, cold-gas thrusters provide rapid stabilization adjustments, including when the vehicle is airborne.
